sections.title: Two objects: to whom, and what
sections.content: *ajánl* ("to recommend") takes two objects: the person you're recommending TO, in the dative (the pronouns *nekem*, *neked*, *neki* from A1, plus *nektek* for "you all", or *-nak/-nek* on a noun: *a barátomnak*, "to my friend"), and the thing recommended, in the accusative -t. *Ajánlok* neked *egy* *kiállítást* means "I recommend an exhibition to you"; *Ajánlok a barátomnak egy kiállítást* means "I recommend an exhibition to my friend".

items.english: I recommend a good exhibition to you.
What do you recommend for this weekend?

sections.content: The person usually comes right after the verb: *ajánlok* NEKED *egy* *kiállítást*. Putting the thing first (*egy* *kiállítást* *ajánlok* neked) is grammatical too, but the first order is the natural, everyday one for a simple recommendation.
